user_input: Seguir com todas as pendencias deixar a parte da licença por ultimo. Implement all missing product, platform, security, observability, and UI capabilities in sequenced batches for the existing Next.js + Spring Boot digital banking MVP. Defer licensing/regulatory work until the final wave, but include technical/regulatory readiness artifacts last. Do not invent a real provider: identify and resolve required provider/API decisions through the normal clarification/architecture/planning gates. Preserve truthful simulation-only behavior until a real, configured BaaS/financial provider integration is available; add contract-level abstractions and test doubles rather than claiming money movement. Prioritize: 1) security/session/recovery/KYC-ready onboarding, 2) real-provider-ready account+ledger+reconciliation+notifications, 3) Pix/transfer/boleto APIs and UI, 4) cards/credit/investments/insurance/support interfaces behind provider abstractions, 5) observability, antifraud/limits/audit/accessibility and 6) licensing/legal readiness last. Use existing code, avoid unrelated rewrites, do not commit. Classification: brownfield upgrade. Change type: upgrade. Project facts: 3,112 nonblank LOC; Java 1,967; JavaScript/TypeScript 1,145; 8 visible top-level directories; 6 git commits; Next.js frontend plus Spring Boot backend; a nested giro-app tree appears duplicated and must be scoped/verified during planning; only CPF/password auth, cookie/JWT flow, disabled mock BaaS account creation, simulated balance/Pix/transfer/bills/scheduling, split calculation without money movement, and local loan/investment calculators currently exist. Feasibility verdict: RISKY due to broad scope and unresolved external financial provider, KYC, notification, Pix/boleto, cards/credit/insurance dependencies; proceed because the user explicitly requested provider decisions through clarification and architecture gates. Record this as proceeding with a known-risk warning.
title: Giro digital banking MVP capability completion

assessment_snapshot.intro: The assessment identifies an existing Next.js and Spring Boot banking MVP that should be completed in-place through provider-safe, sequenced product and platform waves, with a known-risk warning:
bullets: 3,112 nonblank LOC across 1,967 Java and 1,145 JavaScript/TypeScript lines; 8 visible top-level directories; 6 git commits.

Current functionality is limited to CPF/password cookie/JWT auth, disabled mock BaaS account creation, simulated balance/PIX/transfer/bills/scheduling, split calculation, and local loan/investment calculators.
Financial, KYC, notification, Pix/boleto, cards, credit, and insurance provider/API choices remain unresolved and determine major contracts.
A nested giro-app tree appears duplicated and must be verified during planning before implementation scope is fixed.
Licensing/regulatory work is explicitly sequenced last, while technical and regulatory-readiness artifacts must preserve truthful simulation-only claims until configured real providers exist.

proposed_outcome: Complete the existing banking MVP in-place in six ordered waves: security/session/recovery/KYC-ready onboarding; real-provider-ready accounts, ledger, reconciliation, and notifications; Pix/transfer/boleto; provider-abstracted cards, credit, investments, insurance, and support; observability, antifraud, limits, audit, and accessibility; then licensing/legal readiness. Existing behavior and client contracts are preserved unless explicitly changed, all money-movement claims remain simulation-only until a configured provider is available, external dependencies are represented through contracts and test doubles, and unrelated rewrites and commits are avoided.
